title: Given a Scenario, Apply Security Settings on SOHO Wireless and Wired Networks

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: A SOHO router may be the Internet gateway, wireless access point, firewall, DHCP server, and management device. Weak configuration can expose the entire network.
sections.callout: Secure the router → secure Wi-Fi → limit exposure → control access.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When securing a small network, identify whether a router, wireless, firewall, physical, or management setting provides the narrowest effective control.

entries.title: Change Default Passwords
paragraphs: Factory administrator credentials are widely known. Replace them with a strong, unique router password immediately.

entries.title: IP Filtering
paragraphs: Allows or blocks traffic based on source or destination IP addresses, hosts, or networks.

entries.title: Content Filtering
paragraphs: Restricts selected websites, categories, or services for security, parental control, or business policy.
entries.recognitionCue: Block selected sites or categories → content filtering.

entries.title: Firmware Updates
paragraphs: Install vendor firmware updates to correct router security flaws, stability issues, and supported feature problems.

entries.title: Physical Placement/Secure Locations
paragraphs: Keep routers and switches away from public access so unauthorized people cannot reset them, disconnect cables, connect devices, or steal equipment.
entries.recognitionCue: Publicly reachable router → move it to a secure location.

sections.title: Universal Plug and Play (UPnP)
paragraphs: UPnP lets devices and applications discover and request automatic network configuration. It is convenient but can increase exposure and should be disabled when not required.

sections.title: Screened Subnet
paragraphs: A screened subnet isolates externally accessible systems from the protected internal network, similar to a DMZ-style segment.
sections.callout: Public-facing service in a separate network area → screened subnet.

sections.title: Configure Secure Management Access
paragraphs: Protect router administration with HTTPS instead of HTTP, SSH instead of Telnet where applicable, strong credentials, limited management sources, and disabled unnecessary remote administration.
sections.callout: Administrative traffic and credentials must be protected too.

entries.title: Changing the Service Set Identifier (SSID)
paragraphs: Replace the factory wireless name to avoid advertising the router make or model and to identify the network clearly without exposing sensitive information.

entries.title: Disabling SSID Broadcast
paragraphs: Stops ordinary advertisement of the network name but does not provide strong protection because wireless analysis can still discover it.

entries.title: Encryption Settings
paragraphs: Protect wireless traffic with supported secure options such as WPA2 with AES or WPA3 when available.

entries.title: Configuring Guest Access
paragraphs: Gives visitors Internet connectivity while isolating them from trusted internal devices and services.
entries.recognitionCue: Visitor Internet without internal access → guest network.

table.caption: Do not confuse network naming with traffic protection

sections.title: Firewall Settings

entries.title: Disabling Unused Ports
paragraphs: Close or disable ports and services that no system requires to reduce attack surface.
entries.recognitionCue: Nobody needs the service → close the port.

entries.title: Port Forwarding/Mapping
paragraphs: Maps incoming traffic on a router's external interface to a specified internal host and service.

sections.callout: Port forwarding deliberately opens a path inward, so expose only a required and secured service.

table.caption: Choose the correct SOHO control
rows: Visitors must not reach internal resources

sections.title: SOHO Hardening Workflow
bullets: Change default passwords and configure secure management access.
Place network equipment in a secure location.
Use an appropriate SSID, strong encryption, and guest isolation.
Disable unnecessary UPnP and unused ports.
Apply IP and content filtering as required.
Isolate exposed services in a screened subnet.
Use port forwarding only when a secured internal service must be reachable.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Address-based allow or deny → IP filtering
Block sites or categories → content filtering
Protected router administration → secure management access
Stop ordinary name advertisement → disable SSID broadcast

sections.title: Objective 2.10 Exam Trap
bullets: Changing the SSID changes the name; disabling broadcast reduces ordinary visibility; neither replaces encryption.
Guest access isolates visitors from the trusted main WLAN.
UPnP requests configuration automatically; port forwarding is an intentional administrative mapping.
A screened subnet creates a separate area for exposed systems; port forwarding maps traffic through a router or firewall.
Firmware updates change router software; configuration settings change how the router operates.
Unused ports should remain closed; forwarding is only for a required secured service.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: IP allow or deny → IP filtering
sections.callout: Secure the router → secure Wi-Fi → limit exposure → control access.
